ashenvale_commander_spiders.description: She doesn't enjoy asking. She isn't a fool either.
ashenvale_commander_spiders.accept_text:
I don't enjoy asking this of you, and I'd rather say that at the front than have it sit between us for the whole conversation.

My people are stretched from the coast to the Highlands, and you're here. And the forest spiders on the trade road don't care in the slightest whose wagons they take. They've had Sentinel supply and they've had Horde supply, and I understand they took a goblin caravan last month, which is the only part of this I've enjoyed.

So clear the road.

And I'll remember that it was asked and that it was answered. In this forest, that has lately been most of what we have.
ashenvale_commander_spiders.turn_in_text: The road is clear. I'll say this plainly: I didn't expect to thank a Horde blade today. I find that I do.

ashenvale_dryads_gone_quiet.description: They answer when she sings. They haven't answered in a week.
ashenvale_dryads_gone_quiet.accept_text:
The dryads answer when I sing. It isn't a courtesy or training. It's simply how it's always worked here, for as long as there's been a Grove to sing in.

They haven't answered for a week.

I've been down there every evening. I've sung every call they answer, and last night I sang one I'm not supposed to use outside of need, and nothing came.

The corruption is in them now. It won't leave on its own, and it won't leave because I ask it to. I've established both of those at some cost to my dignity.

I'm sorry to ask you to release them. I'm sorrier that I can't do it myself without my voice being the last thing they hear.

Moonwhisper Grove lies east of Astranaar, near the border of the eastern woods. Go and see what has stopped them answering.

ashenvale_furbolg_ravagers.accept_text:
I want to tell you something about the furbolg before you go up that ridge, because nobody your age was taught it.

We've shared this forest with them for a very long time. We were never that formal about it. We both knew where the other's ground was, and in all that time there wasn't a drop of blood between us.

Now the ravagers hold the ridge, and they attack anything that crosses it. They've stopped distinguishing.

Something has changed them, and I've got to get scouts in there to find out what. Thin the ravagers so that becomes possible, and while you're among them, look at them properly. You'll see what I mean.

The ravagers hold the Ragged Highlands, north of Astranaar, past the lake and the Moonwell, in the north-east corner of the forest.
ashenvale_furbolg_ravagers.turn_in_text:
You saw the eyes too, then.

I've had that reported three times and dismissed it twice, because a Sentinel commander who starts talking about what she saw in an animal's eyes gets listened to differently afterwards.

Three is enough. I'm acting on it.

ashenvale_furbolg_shaman_totems.accept_text:
The ravagers aren't the cause. I've been certain of that since the second report, and now I can prove it.

They're being driven from behind. The shamans plant totems in the dens, and the madness is always worst where the totems are thickest. It isn't worst where the fighting is, or at the ridge. It's worst in the dens, at the carvings.

Bring me some of those totems out. And carry them in cloth. I mean that as an order rather than advice. I won't have you holding one of those bare-handed across half a forest to spare yourself the trouble of a wrapping.

The shamans keep to the Ragged Highlands with the rest, north of Astranaar in the north-east corner of the forest.
ashenvale_furbolg_shaman_totems.turn_in_text:
She unwraps one with the cloth still between it and her hand, looks, and covers it again.

That carving isn't furbolg work. I don't know whose it is. I know whose it isn't.

Somebody walked into those dens and gave them this. That changes the question from what happened to the furbolg into who did it to them.

ashenvale_grizzly_problem.description: Bears don't come down to the water to watch a guard post.
ashenvale_grizzly_problem.accept_text:
Bears keep to the trees. A bear wants cover and distance and no part of whatever we're doing. That's what a bear is.

These ones come down to the lake and stand in the open and watch this post. They aren't pacing and they aren't feeding. They stand facing us for as long as it suits them, and then they go back up.

I've held Maestra's Post for eleven years, and I've never once been watched by something that couldn't tell me why.

Put the boldest of them down before one of them walks into Astranaar's market and we find out what the next stage of this is.
ashenvale_grizzly_problem.turn_in_text:
The lake shore's empty, and nothing came down to the water today.

I'd be more relieved if I thought we'd solved it. We've removed the ones brave enough to come and look at us, and that isn't the same as removing the reason they wanted to.

ashenvale_keeper_rustveil.accept_text:
Rustveil kept the Moonwhisper Grove before Astranaar had walls. He kept it longer than that, from before there was anyone here to need walls.

He taught me my first song. I was small enough that he had to bend down to it, and he was patient in a way that nothing that old has any reason to be.

Something has turned him against the forest he watched. I've been to see for myself, and I won't describe it to you, partly to spare you and mostly to spare me.

I'm asking you to put him down. I'm asking it knowing exactly what I'm asking, and I won't dress it up as mercy or duty.

Do it quickly. If anything in him can still know what's happening, I don't want him knowing it for long.
ashenvale_keeper_rustveil.turn_in_text:
Pennarin doesn't ask for any details.

It was quick, then, and I'm glad.

The Grove will choose another keeper eventually. They always do. A grove outlasts whoever is minding it, and I'll be glad of that in a year or so.

Today I'd like to be left alone, and I'd like you to know that isn't ingratitude.

ashenvale_lake_naiads.accept_text:
The naiads have sung to us from Elune'ara for as long as there have been Sentinels on this shore. Nobody ever needed to solve that. It's simply what the lake does.

Lately they sing and then they drag. Two of my fishing party went in last week and came out, and one of them won't go near the water again, and she isn't a woman who frightens.

I won't stand here and say that Lake Elune'ara is a danger. Elune help me, I won't say that out loud about this water.

I'll say that some of its daughters are. Settle them, by the only means they've left anybody.

ashenvale_lake_survey.description: There have been eleven nights of ripples that don't follow the wind.
ashenvale_lake_survey.accept_text:
I keep a ledger of this lake's moods. It isn't a poetic exercise. The Moon Guard have kept one here for generations, and the entries are mostly about weather.

I've counted the ripples from the tower for eleven nights running.

They don't follow the wind, not once in eleven nights, and on two of those nights there was no wind at all and there were still ripples, and they were moving toward the shore rather than along it.

I'd like a second pair of eyes on that shoreline, preferably eyes that aren't mine, because I've been looking at this for eleven nights and I've started to doubt them, and a Moon Guard who doubts his own observations should go and get somebody else's.
ashenvale_lake_survey.turn_in_text: So it's as I thought, and as I'd begun to fear. I'll tell Maestra, and I'll sleep.

ashenvale_night_run_watch.accept_text:
Eltharaen keeps asking me what's on the Night Run. She asks it in that patient way she has, as though I've simply not got round to finding out.

And I keep telling her I don't know, and every time I say it I like myself a little less.

The wagons die on that road. That's the extent of our intelligence. That's what I've got to send up to Astranaar, that wagons die there, which anyone could have told me from the wreckage.

Walk it for me, end to end, all of it. And tell me what that road looks like to someone who isn't afraid of it, because I'm no longer certain I can see it clearly.

The Night Run is the old road in the south-east corner of these woods, a long way from this post, down past the Moonwell and the lake, then east.
ashenvale_night_run_watch.turn_in_text: Wraith-light on the old tree line, you say? Then it's worse than the cats. I'll send for Eltharaen. And I'll find you more work.

ashenvale_nightsaber_thinning.accept_text:
I keep seeing their eyes when I close mine, the cats, in the dark, around the wagon while we were still getting out from under it.

I'm not going to pretend this is about my locket. You've already brought that back, and I'm not owed anything else.

It's that there'll be another family on that road next week. The Night Run is the only way through for anyone coming off the coast, and they'll be doing exactly what we did, at night, because that's when you're told it's safest.

Thin the stalkers before the next wagon tries it.

I'll sleep better. I think rather a lot of people will, and most of them will never know there was anything to sleep badly about, which seems to me the best possible outcome.
ashenvale_nightsaber_thinning.turn_in_text: That's done, then. I'll tell the next wagon driver. He'll pretend not to cry, and then he'll buy you a drink.

ashenvale_refugees_belongings.accept_text:
I know how this sounds. I came off the east coast with a wagon and I lost the wagon, and what I'm asking a stranger to go and find is a piece of jewellery.

It's only silver. It's a painted picture, badly painted, by somebody in a market who charged too much.

It's the only picture of my sister that exists.

The wagon went over on the Night Run, and a cat had it out of the box before I was back on my feet. I'm not asking for the rest. The rest was pots and clothes, and I've made my peace with pots.

Please, just the locket.
ashenvale_refugees_belongings.turn_in_text:
Thessaly opens it and looks at it for a long moment before she closes it again.

That's her, a terrible likeness, and that's her.

Thank you. I've spent three weeks telling myself it was only silver, and I'd very nearly convinced me.

ashenvale_sentinel_scouts_report.accept_text:
Two of mine went up the ridge road toward the Ragged Highlands nine days ago.

They're good, and I want that understood before anything else, because the first thing anyone says is that scouts go missing, and I won't have theirs be the generation that gets shrugged at. They're careful, they're experienced, and I'd have heard from them by now if there were anything at all to hear.

Retrace their route, all of it, as far as the Highlands themselves.

I don't need heroics, and I don't want a rescue attempt. I need to know the point on that road where it stops being safe, because at the moment I'm sending people past it without knowing where it is.
ashenvale_sentinel_scouts_report.turn_in_text:
Shalasyr marks the place on her own map and sits looking at it.

They got that far, then.

So the road is safe right up until it's extremely not, with no warning in between. That's the worst possible answer, and it's the one I needed.

ashenvale_timberling_bark.accept_text:
Look at the posts. Go on, the carved ones at the corners. Do you see the splits running with the grain?

Those are the wards, and they're the only reason this post sleeps at night. Heartwood holds a ward the way nothing I can requisition does. I've tried iron, I've tried stone, and I've tried asking Astranaar nicely, which was the least effective of the three.

The timberlings in Silverwind Vale carry it in their chests.

And before you ask me to be gentle about it, they came through my fence line last spring and they weren't gentle with it, and I've a very long memory for fences.
ashenvale_timberling_bark.turn_in_text:
She runs a thumb along the fresh grain.

That's good wood. That'll hold a season, maybe two.

I'd rather be carving these because the old ones wore out than because something's been testing them. That's twice now this week I've wanted a different reason for a job.

ashenvale_ursal_the_mauler.accept_text:
Shalasyr sends word the totems are done, which is what I needed. Then whatever was feeding the Highland bears has stopped, and Ursal has nothing left driving him but his own temper, which, to be fair to him, has always been considerable.

He's the biggest of them, and he's the one herding the others down toward the lake. That's been the shape of it all along. He moves, and they move.

Go and finish it. And do something for me. Before you do it, get a proper look at his eyes, and then come back and tell me honestly whether they were a bear's. I've asked three people that question, and every one of them changed the subject.

He dens in the Ragged Highlands, east of this post.
ashenvale_ursal_the_mauler.turn_in_text:
She listens to your answer and doesn't react for a while.

Thank you for saying it plainly.

Then he was being ridden, at the end, and he had been for a long time, and every one of those bears we put down at the shore was somebody else's hand moving. I'll carry that. It's better than not knowing.

ashenvale_wisp_lights.accept_text:
The wisps are the Grove's lanterns. That isn't poetry. It's their function, and it's why the Grove is lit at all.

They're old, older than the trees in some cases, and there's an argument, which I happen to believe, that they remember who planted this place.

They're flickering, not dying out, the way a lamp does when something is wrong with the fuel rather than the wick, and I want the healers to have something to work from before it becomes the other thing.

Bring me what falls from them as they fade. And listen to me carefully: don't take a mote that hasn't fallen, not one. I'll know, and so will the Grove, and I'm genuinely unsure which of us would be worse about it.
ashenvale_wisp_lights.turn_in_text:
She holds a vial up and watches it pulse.

They're all fallen. I did check, and I'd have thought less of myself for checking if I'd found you'd done it properly and never said.

The healers can work with this. Whatever's in the Grove, it's in the light first.

ashenvale_wraith_toll.accept_text:
Now I know what's on it, I can tell you what's wrong with it.

The dead of the Night Run don't want revenge. People assume they do, because people assume a hostile dead thing must have a grievance, and it makes the road easier to think about.

They want company, and nothing more. Every wagon that goes down that road is a crowd of warm people passing through a place where something is extremely alone, and they take a toll because taking is the only way they know to ask.

Understanding it doesn't help the carters. End the ones on the road, and the rest might remember they were people and settle.
ashenvale_wraith_toll.turn_in_text:
The road's open. There's a wagon due through from the coast tomorrow, and I'm going to let it go.

It's the first time in four months I've signed off on that without feeling like I was spending someone.

lumber_elder_stump.accept_text:
There's a stump out there that walks.

I've cut forty years of trees. I've taken things down that were old when my grandfather's clan came over the sea, and I've never minded it. A tree's a tree and a camp's a camp, and I sleep like a stone.

That one's the oldest thing in this forest, and it guards the last good stand, and I've never in my life wanted something gone so badly.

I'm not going to dress that up as duty. It's the quota, and it's also that it stood and looked at me across the cut for an hour last week and I haven't slept right since.

Fell it for me. The camp will drink to it, and I'll be buying. The crews call it the Elder Timberling.
lumber_elder_stump.turn_in_text: It actually fell? Hah, the whole camp will hear about this! Take the sap. It's good for something, I'm sure.

lumber_felling_season.accept_text:
A good tree dies in four swings. I've timed it, I've trained it, and I've built a camp's whole work rate around it.

These walkers take it back with a root in the ear.

The timberlings stand with the stand east of camp, and they don't let a crew near it. They're patient about it. They don't charge. They just put themselves between my boys and the trunk until somebody loses their temper, and then it's a funeral.

Clear them off so my crews can work. And don't leave any standing. I've tried leaving a few, and they fetch more.
lumber_felling_season.turn_in_text: That's the stand clear. I owe you a few logs' worth of thanks. Have one of the leftover axes. They aren't good, but they're mine.

lumber_silk_slings.accept_text:
Rope breaks, and that isn't a complaint, it's an engineering fact, and every log-sling in this camp is rope, and every one of them will eventually part under a full oak.

Silk doesn't break.

The forest spiders out here are bigger than they've any business being, and so is their silk. The strands come off them thick as a bootlace, and you can't cut one with a belt knife. I've tried, in front of witnesses.

Bring me bundles of it, enough to weave slings with.

I'll lift a whole oak in one piece, and I'll do it in front of the Overseer, who's been telling me for two years that it can't be done with the crew I've got.

raynewood_cats.description: She doesn't welcome strangers. The cats don't distinguish either.
raynewood_cats.accept_text:
I don't generally welcome strangers to this retreat. I certainly don't generally welcome the Horde, and I'd rather say so to your face than have you find it out in my manner.

The nightsabers don't distinguish.

They've stopped respecting the quiet here. Raynewood has kept a boundary for a very long time without a fence. The cats knew where it was and kept to the other side of it, and now they come through it at dusk, and they come as far as the door.

Drive them off.

When it's done the retreat can go back to being quiet, and you and I can go back to our respective positions on each other, which I think we'd both prefer.
raynewood_cats.turn_in_text: The retreat is quiet. I haven't been grateful to a stranger in years, and I'm grateful now.

raynewood_dryads.description: They sleep, and what wakes in them isn't them.
raynewood_dryads.accept_text:
The dryads here have gone to sleep. That by itself would be no cause for alarm. They do sleep, deeply, for longer than you'd credit.

What wakes in them isn't them.

I've watched it happen twice now. The sleep goes on too long, and then there's movement, and what gets up moves wrong from the first step. There's nothing of the dryad left in it by the time it's standing.

Put them to rest rather than leave them to that. I'd do it myself, and I want that said, but my hands aren't what they used to be, and this isn't work to do badly.

Please be quick. And not while they're still sleeping, if you can help it. Let them be asleep.
raynewood_dryads.turn_in_text: I'll light a candle for each. Thank you for doing what I couldn't. It will be remembered at Raynewood.

raynewood_vigil_lights.accept_text:
We keep a vigil here for the ones the forest has lost. I don't mean the fallen. I mean the lost, and that's a longer list: the ones who went into the corruption and didn't come out and were never found to be buried.

It's lit with wisp-light, and it has been since before Raynewood had a roof.

The wisps give it freely, if you ask them. That's the entire method, and I'm aware of how it sounds to somebody who arrived this morning with an axe.

So ask them. Stand still, and ask, and take what they let fall.

If you take a light that wasn't offered, the vigil will still light. It simply won't mean anything, and I'd be the only one who knew, and I'd know for years.

splintertree_blood_orders.accept_text:
Cultists carry orders. All of them do, and the Burning Blade are no exception, because somebody has to tell them where to stand and when.

And a cultist never carries anything he can't hide behind a knife, which means the orders are on them, and they're small, and they'll be destroyed the moment one of them decides a fight is going badly.

So be quick about it. That's the whole of my tactical advice. Be quick, and go through them before the ink has a chance to meet any blood.

Bring me the scraps. I don't care what the orders say, because orders are always the same four sentences. I care about the hand. Somebody is writing these, and a hand I can match is a person I can find.
splintertree_blood_orders.turn_in_text: Written in blood and signed in ash. Whoever's behind this wants to be found, eventually. I'd rather be ready.

splintertree_burning_blade_scouts.description: Kill the scouts, and the ritual circles can't hide.
splintertree_burning_blade_scouts.accept_text:
Cultists poke about the Wastes like rats in a cellar, and like rats they're only interesting for what they lead you to.

The Burning Blade are putting up ritual circles out there. I can't find them. The Wastes are big and a circle is small, and these people aren't stupid about where they put them.

But I don't need to find the circles. I need to find the guards, and guards stand near the thing they're guarding, which is the single most reliable fact in the practice of war.

Kill their scouts along the Wastes' edge. Wherever you have to kill a lot of them in one place, that's a circle, and then I can finish my map.
splintertree_burning_blade_scouts.turn_in_text: That many of them? They guard more than I thought. I'll mark it on the map and show Vashj. You have the hands for this. I hope you have the stomach, too.

splintertree_demon_wastes_watch.description: From the wall she sees smoke. From the ground you see who lit it.
splintertree_demon_wastes_watch.accept_text:
From this wall, I see smoke, every night, from somewhere out in the Wastes, and I've logged the position of it the best I can from up here.

From the ground, you see who lit it.

That's the whole difference between my job and the job I'm asking you to do, and I'd swap if I could. But if I come off this wall there's nobody on it, and an empty wall is just a fence.

Walk the edge of the Wastes, and come back and tell me what's burning and who's standing round it.

I'll keep the wall warm. That's a joke. It's the only one I've got, and I've been working on it for two weeks.
splintertree_demon_wastes_watch.turn_in_text: Smoke without a fire, you say? Some things burn the other way. I'll tell Gorada. She'll curse a lot.

splintertree_fel_imp_cache.description: They stack what they steal, and it isn't a nest.
splintertree_fel_imp_cache.accept_text:
They take hinges, buckles, a strip of my own mess-tent canvas, cut square.

The imps carry off the dumbest things out of this outpost and stack them in the dirt out in the Wastes, and I've been going out there to look at the stacks, which I'd rather you didn't mention to the War Mage.

It isn't a nest. I've seen nests and I've seen hoards, and this is neither. It's arranged, the same way every time, and a thief doesn't arrange.

I think it's a message, and I think nobody told us how to read it. Bring me scraps off them, enough that I can lay it out the way they do and look at the whole of it at once.

The imps nest in the Demon Wastes, east of here. Whatever they're carrying, I want it back.
splintertree_fel_imp_cache.turn_in_text: That's the hinge off my own tent flap, right enough. The mess-tent has to stay up, and the imps have to stay out. Don't tell Sergeant Krull it was imps. He'll ask me why we couldn't stop them.

splintertree_lord_malgan.accept_text:
A tyrant who loses a ritual has two choices open to him. He can try again, or die trying.

I've buried enough grunts to know which one Malgan will pick, and I've no intention of letting him get far enough into it to find out whether I'm right.

He holds the Throne by fear now rather than by strength. Those aren't the same thing, and the satyrs under him know it even if he doesn't. You can hear it in how they move when he's in the open.

So I'll make the choice for him. He's at the Throne. Go and take it away from him.

Satyr's Throne is north of Splintertree. He hasn't left it, and he won't.

splintertree_pit_lord_emissary.accept_text:
It arrived with terms.

It's been standing in the Wastes for two days waiting for somebody of appropriate rank to come out and receive them, and in that time three of my scouts have gone close enough to hear the opening and come back changed in ways I'm still assessing.

I don't read the terms of things that stand in fire. There's no version of this where we hear it out and come away with more than we started with. An emissary's entire function is to make the next thing sound reasonable.

Cut it off before it finishes a sentence, preferably the first one.

It's waiting in the Demon Wastes, east of the post, for our answer. Take it one.
splintertree_pit_lord_emissary.turn_in_text: It was still talking when you reached it? Of course it was. They always are. I'll burn what's left of the terms.

splintertree_satyr_ritual.description: They've been singing for three nights, and it isn't a welcome.
splintertree_satyr_ritual.accept_text:
The satyrs at Satyr's Throne have been singing for three nights.

I've fought a great many things in this forest, and I've learned their songs the way you learn any language, by listening to it being used for ordinary purposes until the unusual ones stand out.

That song isn't a welcome. It isn't mourning either, which was my second guess and which I'd have preferred.

It's a song of preparation. Something is being made ready at the Throne, and the tricksters are leading the chant, which means the tricksters are the part that has to be carried.

Remove them, and the song has nothing to carry it, and whatever is being prepared stays unprepared a while longer.
splintertree_satyr_ritual.turn_in_text: The chant has stopped, for tonight, anyway. You did well. Whoever commands them will be furious. I'd like to meet him on my terms.

splintertree_timber_quota.accept_text:
Orgrimmar wants timber, and I want my loggers alive. For most of my career those have been the same objective, and lately they haven't been.

The grizzlies have decided the stand north-west of here, up at the Warsong Lumber Camp, is theirs. They come in at the crews, in daylight, which bears don't do unless something is very wrong with the arrangement they'd normally keep with us.

Deal with the biggest of them.

And before you suggest it, yes, I could send word to the Warchief and ask for the quota to be adjusted on account of bears. I'm told he's very reasonable about this sort of thing.

That's precisely why I'm asking you instead.
splintertree_timber_quota.turn_in_text: That's done, and the quota's back on track. You're hired, though not formally. I don't do paperwork, but I'll remember your name.

splintertree_twilight_acolytes.accept_text:
Something under the Barrow is listening, and the acolytes are the ones doing the talking.

They go out at night and whisper to the buried dead. They don't chant. They whisper, the way you'd talk to somebody through a door, and you can stand on the mound and hear the shape of it without catching a word.

I don't know what's down there. I want to be extremely clear that I don't intend to find out by letting the conversation continue until it answers.

Silence the acolytes. Whatever is under that mound can go back to being a thing nobody has spoken to in a thousand years.

The Twilight Barrow is north-east of Splintertree, at the eastern edge of the forest.
splintertree_twilight_acolytes.turn_in_text: It's quiet, and that's good. I felt it go quiet from the walls. Whatever was down there has lost its mouthpieces, for now.

splintertree_twilight_overseer.description: Every cult has someone who isn't a believer.
splintertree_twilight_overseer.accept_text:
Every cult has somebody in it who isn't a believer, only a boss.

You can pick him out at a distance if you know what to look for. He's the one who doesn't look up during the important part. The acolytes were whispering for somebody, and it was him.

Kill him and the rest scatter, or they come for you, which is a better fight than the one we'll be having if whatever is under that Barrow learns to speak for itself.

I'd rather fight a hundred frightened cultists than one patient thing underground with a voice.

You'll find him where you found the acolytes, at the Twilight Barrow, north-east of Splintertree.
splintertree_twilight_overseer.turn_in_text: I can feel the Barrow settling. That was well done. Now we only have to worry about everything else.

splintertree_voidwalkers.accept_text:
The remnants drift through the Demon Wastes, east of this wall, after dark.

They aren't alive. They aren't dead either, and I've had that argument with a priest and won it. They weren't made for the world. That's the nearest I can get. Something summoned them here and then stopped paying attention, and they've been bumping along the inside of a place that doesn't want them ever since.

They're drifting closer to the wall every night. I've marked it.

Disperse them out there, before they get close enough to find out how thin this wall actually is. I know how thin it is. I'd prefer to keep that between us.

splintertree_wraiths.accept_text:
I've buried four recruits this week, four of them, and they were four I trained myself, which I mention not for sympathy but so you understand I'm not reading this off a casualty list.

There are wraiths in the timber east of the post. They come at the woodcutting details, and the details are exactly the wrong people to meet them: axes, no shields, and half of them are nineteen.

I want them back in the dirt.

And don't say it. I've had three separate people explain to me this week that they're already dead, as though that were a clever observation that hadn't occurred to me, and the next one to say it digs the graves.
splintertree_wraiths.turn_in_text: Seven of them? I can't say good job in front of the recruits, so I'll say it here. That was a good job.

zoram_crab_traps.accept_text:
The crabs got bold when the naga started wandering the shallows.

That's the order it happened in, and I'll stand by it. The naga came, everything else in the water had a worse thing to worry about than me, and now the big shore crabs take my traps and crush them against the rocks for no reason I can determine beyond that they can.

I've been rebuilding traps for a month. I'm an old man who spends his days making boxes for crabs to destroy, which wasn't the retirement I'd sketched out.

Thin out the big ones. Then I'll be able to eat dinner like a free man instead of like a crab's tenant.

zoram_lookout_bluffs.description: She watches the water so the others can sleep. She hasn't slept in days.
zoram_lookout_bluffs.accept_text:
I watch the water so the rest of them can sleep. That's the posting, and I've never resented it.

I watch the water, and lately the water watches back. I've had several days to find a better way of saying it, and that's still the most accurate one available.

Here's my actual problem, stripped of all that. I can't see the Coast Bluffs from this post. There's a shoulder of rock in the way and there always has been, and for years that didn't matter.

I think that's where it's coming from. Go up there and walk them.

And if it's nothing, if it's birds and surf and a tired Sentinel, then come back and tell me that, and I'll go to sleep for about a day and a half.

zoram_murloc_nets.accept_text:
I've fished this strand for forty years.

In all that time the murlocs never touched a line of mine. We had an arrangement, near enough. They worked the shallows, I worked the deep, and if one of them got into the net he came out again and we both pretended it hadn't happened.

Now they're cutting my nets, with bone knives, deliberately, from underneath, in the dark, and leaving the fish.

They aren't hungry. That's the part that's had me awake. A hungry murloc takes the fish.

Deal with the spearfishers for me. And when you're back I'll tell you the story of the big silverfin, which is an extremely good story, and which nobody on this coast will sit still for any more.
zoram_murloc_nets.turn_in_text: That's ten of them! My boy, my nets will live. Now sit, sit, about the silverfin. It was longer than a dock, and it winked.

zoram_naga_coastguard.accept_text:
I build a boat in a week, and they sink it in a night.

That's three this month. I'm most of the way through a fourth, and I've reached the point where I'm building it slowly on purpose, because finishing it means finding out whether it lasts till morning.

The coastguards come in off the reef after dark. They don't take anything and they don't come ashore. They hole the hulls and go back out.

I'm not asking you to be brave about it. Bravery's no use to me. I had a nephew who was brave about it, and I'd rather have had the boat and the nephew.

I'm asking you to be efficient. Drive them off the reef.
zoram_naga_coastguard.turn_in_text: As many as that? I'll build the fourth boat a little faster, then. You'll forgive me if I name it after you. I name them all after people who've been useful.

zoram_tidecaller_pearls.accept_text:
Here's the thing nobody at Zoram'gar will sit still long enough to hear.

The tidecallers don't carry weapons, not one. I've been close enough to be sure of it, closer than I'd choose to be again.

They carry pearls, and the water answers them.

I build boats. That means I spend my life working out what water will do and planning around it, and I'm telling you water isn't supposed to do what it does when one of those things holds a pearl up.

Bring some back. I want to know what a pearl is made of that it can do that, and whether it keeps doing it once it's out of a naga's hand. If it does, I can stop building boats that sink and start building ones that argue back.
zoram_tidecaller_pearls.turn_in_text: Nothing pearl-like should hum, so these can't be pearls. I'm going to find out what they are, and I'm going to be very quiet about it.
